cities.base: Between Odori and Susukino, Minami 1 to Minami 4, on the Namboku line. Everything you eat is within fifteen minutes on foot, the airport train is twelve minutes' walk north, and you do not need the ca
cities.name: Sapporo

cities.base: Ironai or Hanazono, between the station and the canal. One night is enough and it gets you the sushi counters after the Sapporo day-trippers have taken the 17:00 train back.
cities.name: Otaru

cities.base: Lower Hirafu, near the crossroads at Hirafu-zaka, where the handful of restaurants that stay open in summer are; Kutchan town is cheaper and duller and needs the car for everything.
cities.name: Niseko Hirafu

cities.base: Furano town within ten minutes of the station, which puts Kumagera and Yuiga Doxon on foot and Farm Tomita fifteen minutes north by car; in the third week of July book months ahead because there are n
cities.name: Furano

cities.base: Not a base. The patchwork hills, Shikisai no Oka and the Shirogane Blue Pond are a loop of about 90 km driven from Furano in a day; sleeping in Biei town buys nothing but a shorter drive to the pond.
cities.name: Biei hills and the Blue Pond

cities.base: A nature bed. Utoro, the west-side village where every road into the park starts. The onsen hotels on the hill above the port are worth the price for one night of half board.
cities.name: Utoro, Shiretoko

places.name: Sapporo Curb Market (Jogai Ichiba)
places.note: About 60 stalls outside the wholesale market with kaisen-don for 2,500 to 4,000 yen, cheaper and less worked-over than Nijo; the wholesale market behind it is shut Sundays and most of the outer stalls take Sunday off too, and the crab sellers will steer you to the priciest tank.

places.name: Nijo Market
places.note: Skip it: a one-block market ten minutes from Odori where uni-don has crossed 5,000 yen and the touts work in English; the Curb Market does the same bowl for half and the fish came off the same truck.

places.name: Soup Curry Garaku
places.note: The queue is real, 30 to 60 minutes at noon, for a soup curry that is worth one wait in your life; pick the chicken leg, spice level 3 or 4, and go at 11:20 or after 14:00.

places.name: Jingisukan Daruma Honten
places.note: Twenty stools round a counter since 1954, fresh lamb on a domed grill, no reservations and a line from 17:00; the 6.4 and 4.4 branches nearby have the same lamb and shorter waits, and your clothes will smell of it tomorrow.

places.name: Sumire Nakanoshima Honten
places.note: The shop that set Sapporo miso ramen in its current form, ten minutes' walk from Nakanoshima subway, with a film of lard that keeps the bowl scalding to the last noodle; hours have shifted between sources, so treat the mid-afternoon as the risky window.

places.name: Ramen Shingen Minami 6-jo
places.note: Open to 01:00, the miso bowl every Sapporo office worker names first, and the line moves; the sensible answer to a late night in Susukino.

places.name: Sapporo Beer Museum and tasting hall
places.note: The 1890 red-brick brewery with a self-guided floor for 1,000 yen and a three-beer tasting set for 1,200 downstairs; the premium guided tour is not run on Mondays and the whole place shuts only on 31 December.

places.name: Sapporo Beer Garden, Kessel Hall
places.note: All-you-can-eat Genghis Khan and beer for 100 minutes under a brewing kettle from 1912, about 4,500 yen; loud, tourist-heavy and still a good night, and without a reservation the wait at 18:30 is over an hour.

places.name: Moerenuma Park
places.note: Isamu Noguchi's last work, a landfill turned into a 62 m grass mountain, a glass pyramid and a sea fountain that fires two to four times a day from late April to mid-October; bus 69 or 79 from Kanjodori-higashi, and rent a bicycle at the east gate because it is nearly two km across.

places.name: Mt Moiwa ropeway at dusk
places.note: Tram to Ropeway Iriguchi, free shuttle, two lifts to 531 m and the whole grid lit below; go for the last light rather than full dark and expect the return car to be a crush at 20:00 in summer.

places.name: Historical Village of Hokkaido
places.note: Fifty-two Meiji and Taisho buildings moved to a forest park, with a horse tram in summer; open daily May to September and closed Mondays the rest of the year, and it is a train plus a bus so give it a half day.

places.name: Hokkaido Museum of Modern Art
places.note: A 510 yen permanent collection strong on Hokkaido painters and Pasquin, quiet on a wet afternoon; closed Mondays, and the special shows cost extra.

places.name: Otaru Canal, the Asakusa bridge end
places.note: A 1923 canal with stone warehouses along one bank and a promenade that is a coach stop by day; the 63 gas lamps come on at dusk and by 19:30 the crowd has gone back to Sapporo.

places.name: Bank of Japan Otaru Museum
places.note: The 1912 branch by Tatsuno Kingo, the man who did Tokyo Station, kept as a free museum of the years Otaru was the Wall Street of the north; closed Wednesdays, not Mondays, which catches people out.

places.name: Otaru Masazushi Honten
places.note: The oldest counter on Sushi Street, open since 1938, with a 5,000 yen lunch set that is the sensible way to eat Otaru fish; closed Wednesdays and full by 12:15 in summer.

places.name: Miyofuku
places.note: Eight seats, one couple, about 3,000 yen for a set of nigiri that locals rate above the famous names; closed Sundays, cash, and no English menu, so point at what the man next to you is having.

places.name: Shakotan Cuisine Fujizushi, Sakaimachi
places.note: Uni chirashi from the Shakotan peninsula, the reason to be here in June, July or August, at about 3,500 yen; outside May to August the uni is frozen or absent, and the shop says so.

places.name: Wakadori Jidai Naruto Honten
places.note: Half a chicken deep-fried in a 1957 canteen three blocks from the station, the Otaru dish that is not fish; open daily 11:00 to 20:30 and a fifteen-minute wait at 18:00.

places.name: Kitaichi Hall
places.note: A stone warehouse lit by 167 oil lamps, coffee and cake for about 1,100 yen; the lamps are lit from 08:45 and the only quiet hour is the first one, before the glass shops next door open.

places.name: Sakaimachi Street
places.note: The 900 m of Meiji bank and merchant buildings that is now glass, music boxes and LeTAO cheesecake, wall to wall from 11:00 to 16:00; walk it early for the buildings and skip the Music Box Museum, which is a shop.

places.name: Kamaei kamaboko, Sakaimachi factory shop
places.note: Fish cake made in the open kitchen since 1905, fried to order for 300 to 400 yen a stick; the panju cheese one is the walking snack for the canal.

places.name: Tenguyama ropeway
places.note: Four minutes to 532 m, the harbour and Ishikari Bay below and chipmunks in a pen at the top, 1,800 yen return; bus 9 from the station, and the summer season runs 25 April to 3 November with cars to 21:00 for the lights.

places.name: Otaru Kihinkan, the Old Aoyama Villa at Shukutsu
places.note: A herring baron's house built 1917 to 1923 in zelkova wood, with sliding doors painted by Kawai Gyokudo; 1,300 yen, 300 for the garden only, 09:00 to 17:00. No photos inside, very cold in winter, and winter hours are not confirmed, so check.

places.name: Sankaku Market
places.note: Skip it: a corridor of crab tanks against the station wall where a kaisen-don costs what a sushi lunch does on Sushi Street, aimed entirely at the tour buses.

places.name: Shinsen-numa boardwalk
places.note: A 3 km boardwalk loop round a high marsh at 760 m, 25 minutes from Hirafu up the Panorama Line, with Yotei across the valley on a clear morning; the road is shut from late October to late April.

places.name: Goshiki Onsen
places.note: Milky sulphur water in wooden tubs at 750 m with the Niseko range over the fence, 800 yen and tattoo-tolerant; summer hours 09:00 to 20:00, towel hire 300 yen.

places.name: Mt Yotei, Makkari trailhead
places.note: The gentlest way up the 1,898 m volcano and still 1,670 m of gain over 13.4 km, nine hours car to car with a hut but no water above the trailhead. July to September, start by 06:00; it is out of season now.

places.name: Kyogoku Fukidashi Park
places.note: Where 80,000 tonnes a day of Yotei snowmelt come out of a lava wall into a mossy pool, 20 minutes east of Hirafu; free, cold, and every local car has empty bottles in the boot for it.

places.name: Niseko Milk Kobo, Takahashi Farm
places.note: Cream puffs and soft serve made from the farm's own milk, 300 to 500 yen, with Yotei across the pasture; open daily, and the queue in August is worth ten minutes and not thirty.

places.name: Kamimura
places.note: Yuichi Kamimura's tasting menu of Hokkaido produce, dinner from 18:00, closed Sundays. Wanderlog and a Tripadvisor title now say it has closed while 2024 guides still list it, so check it is taking bookings before you count on it.

places.name: A Bu Cha 2
places.note: The izakaya in a converted farmhouse that half of Hirafu eats in, hotpot and grilled fish for about 5,000 yen a head; limited summer opening and closed Mondays, so check the door before you count on it.

places.name: Bar Gyu+, the fridge door
places.note: You enter through a 1950s refrigerator door into a room of Japanese whisky and jazz; in summer it has kept to Thursday to Saturday nights only, so the other four nights it is dark.

places.name: Yukoro onsen
places.note: The plain neighbourhood bath at the bottom of the village, 800 yen, outdoor tub under the trees; the answer to the Yotei day when you cannot face a drive to Goshiki.

places.name: Grand Hirafu summer gondola
places.note: The ski gondola runs in summer to 820 m for the full-face view of Yotei and a 2 to 3 hour return walk to the 1,308 m Annupuri summit; it stops in rain and wind and the schedule changes yearly. The summer run is over, so it is shut now.

places.name: Lake Toya and the 20:45 fireworks
places.note: An hour south to a caldera lake with a hot-spring strip; about 450 fireworks go up from a boat nightly from 28 April to 31 October at 20:45, free from the shore, so they are over for this year. The Usuzan ropeway, 1,800 yen, shows the 2000 eruption scars.

places.name: Shiribetsu River rafting with NAC
places.note: Summer rafting on the Shiribetsu is a gentle grade 2 float with a few splashes, 6,500 yen or so for a half day, run by the outfit that has done it since 1995; the May snowmelt trip is the rough one. The season is over, so it is shut now.

places.name: Farm Tomita
places.note: The original lavender farm, free, twelve hectares in stripes with the Tokachi peaks behind, at its purple peak for about three weeks from early July; be in the car park by 08:30 or you share it with fifty coaches.

places.name: Lavender East
places.note: Tomita's 14-hectare overflow field 4 km east, open in July and the first days of August, with a 200 yen tractor bus through the rows and a fraction of the crowd; the season is over, so it is shut now.

places.name: Hinode Park lavender hill
places.note: The town-run lavender slope above Kamifurano with a bell on top and the Tokachi range in front, free and empty next to Tomita; the same three-week bloom in July, so it is out of season now.

places.name: Kumagera
places.note: Furano wagyu roast beef bowl and venison nabe in a log-walled room five minutes from the station, about 3,500 yen at dinner; closed Wednesdays and full by 18:30 in July, so book or arrive at 17:30.

places.name: Yuiga Doxon
places.note: Homemade sausage and curry in a dark wooden room the writer of the television drama Kita no Kuni Kara used to eat in; closed Mondays, lunch until 15:30 on weekdays, and the curry is the order.

places.name: Furano Cheese Factory
places.note: Free to look at the camembert line through glass, then a pizza from the wood oven and an ice cream, about 1,500 yen; the squid-ink black cheese is a gift, not a lunch. Open daily except the New Year break.

places.name: Furano Winery
places.note: The city-owned winery on the hill above town with free tastings of an honest, slightly thin Furano red and a view down the valley; better as a 30-minute stop than a destination.

places.name: Furano Marche
places.note: The town's food hall of local producers, melon by the slice, Furano cheese, a good bakery, five minutes from the station. Open 10:00 to 18:00, to 19:00 from mid-June to late August; closed from mid-November and on 31 December and 1 January, so likely shut for a November stay.

places.name: Ningle Terrace
places.note: Fifteen log-cabin craft shops on a boardwalk through the woods below the Prince hotel, lit at night; pleasant for 40 minutes after dinner and nothing you need to buy.

places.name: Ryounkaku day bath, Tokachidake Onsen
places.note: The highest onsen in Hokkaido at 1,280 m, 45 minutes up from Furano, with a brown iron-rich outdoor bath looking straight at the smoking Tokachi crater; day use is about 1,000 yen and the road is clear May to October.

places.name: Furano Ropeway summer run
places.note: The ski gondola to 900 m for the whole valley and the Tokachi range in one view, and a short walk at the top; summer operation is weekends and holidays plus daily in July and August, varies by year, and the summer run is over now.

places.name: Shirogane Blue Pond
places.note: An accidental 1988 flood-control pond turned cobalt by aluminium in the water, the most photographed thing in Hokkaido and a ten-minute look; 500 yen parking, the car park queue starts about 10:00 in July, and grey skies dull the blue.

places.name: Shirahige Falls
places.note: Groundwater falling in white threads out of a lava cliff into a blue river, seen from the road bridge three minutes above the pond; free, always open, and better than the pond on a cloudy day.

places.name: Shikisai no Oka
places.note: Seven hectares of flower stripes on a hillside south of town, free to walk, with a 500 yen tractor-train and an alpaca pen; heaving from 11:00, so make it the last stop of the day when the light comes in low.

places.name: Patchwork Road: Ken and Mary tree to Hokusei Hill
places.note: A 15 km loop of rolling wheat and potato fields north of Biei named for cigarette adverts of the 1970s, with the pyramid lookout at Hokusei no Oka to end on; drive it, stop where the pull-offs are, and do not walk into anyone's field.

places.name: Zerubu no Oka
places.note: The flower field on the north loop, free entry with a 500 yen buggy track, and the one that has Yotei-shaped Asahidake behind it on a clear day; ten minutes from the station.

places.name: Takushinkan, the Shinzo Maeda gallery
places.note: The photographer who made these hills famous in the 1970s has his prints in an old schoolhouse in a birch wood; free, and it explains what you have been looking at all day. Hours shorten to 10:00 to 16:00 in winter.

places.name: Biei Senka
places.note: The farmers' shop and restaurant on the main road north of town, corn and asparagus in season, a 1,500 yen lunch of local vegetables and a good ice cream; the lunch queue is short before noon.

places.name: Shirogane Onsen day baths
places.note: Three hotels below the Blue Pond sell day baths of iron-brown water for 1,000 to 1,300 yen, mostly 12:00 to 16:00; the useful hour after the pond and the falls, before the drive back to Furano.

places.name: Biei town and the Kamikawa flower road bakeries
places.note: The stone-fronted main street by the station, kept low by an old town ordinance, with two bakeries and a coffee roaster in walking distance; a 30-minute break between the north hills and the pond.

places.name: Shiretoko Goko elevated boardwalk
places.note: An 800 m raised walkway fenced with electric wire to a deck over Lake One with the Shiretoko range behind, free, no guide, no bear closures, about 40 minutes from Utoro, parking 500 yen. The season is mid-April to mid-November, so it shuts for winter now.

places.name: Shiretoko Goko ground loop, the long course
places.note: The 3 km forest loop past all five lakes; from 10 May to 31 July it is guided-only, about 6,000 yen with 10-minute departures and a bear briefing, and from 1 August a 450 yen lecture and you walk it yourself. It closes on the spot when a bear is seen.

places.name: Furepe Falls walk from the Nature Center
places.note: Two km of easy trail through meadow and forest to a 100 m sea cliff where groundwater weeps into the Okhotsk, deer everywhere; free, and the Nature Center at the trailhead lends bear spray and posts the day's sightings.

places.name: Kamuiwakka hot falls
places.note: A warm sulphur river you climb barefoot for 500 m over three falls to a fourth, 30 to 45 minutes up; July to September only, 2,900 yen with a timed online reservation. The road is shut for the winter now, and in Obon a shuttle replaces private cars.

places.name: Shiretoko Pass
places.note: The 738 m pass on the only road across the peninsula, with Rausu-dake above and Kunashiri on the horizon; free, a public road and viewpoint with free parking. A 23.8 km stretch closes from late October to late April, so it is shut now, and it is fogged in more mornings than not.

places.name: Rausu whale and dolphin cruise
places.note: Two and a half hours in the Nemuro Strait with Shiretoko Nature Cruise or Gojiraiwa Kanko, 8,800 yen, for sperm whales, Baird's beaked whales, dolphins and, in June and July, orcas; late April to mid-October, a 45-minute drive from Utoro, and no refund for a whale-free day.

places.name: Gojiraiwa Kanko bear-watching boat to Rusha
places.note: A small fast boat up the west coast to Rusha Bay where brown bears fish the river mouth, about two hours and 8,000 yen; late April to October, best July to September, and it does not run in a north swell.

places.name: Oshinkoshin Falls
places.note: An 80 m double waterfall beside the road ten minutes south of Utoro, with 200 steps to a platform; free, no gate, free parking, open all hours all year. The souvenir shop keeps 09:00 to 17:00 and closes Wednesday. Worth exactly twenty minutes.

places.name: Utoro Gyokyo Fujinbu Shokudo
places.note: The fishermen's wives' canteen on the harbour since 1965: salmon oyakodon 1,800 yen, uni-don 2,500 yen but only May to August, from 08:30 until the fish runs out around 14:00. Closed Thursday, one listing says Sunday too; cash only, and winter opening is not confirmed.

places.name: Maruko Suisan
places.note: The fishmonger's kaisen-don counter next to the port, the other lunch in a village with few, about 3,000 yen with crab; 10:30 to 15:30 and 17:00 to 20:30 daily, but shut when the boats do not go out, so have the shokudo as a fallback.

places.name: Yuhidai no Yu public onsen
places.note: The village's outdoor bath on the sunset hill, 500 yen, open June to October from 14:00 to 20:00, so it is shut now until June; if your hotel has no spring this is the bath, and a good one even if it does.

places.name: Kuma no Yu, Rausu
places.note: A free, volunteer-kept outdoor bath in the trees above Rausu, men and women separate, water hot enough to hurt; take a donation, keep quiet, and get in slowly. Combine with the whale boat.

places.name: Sapporo Clock Tower
places.note: Built in 1878 as the drill hall of Sapporo Agricultural College, now an Important Cultural Property, and the 1881 American clock still runs. A small history museum with English text, 30 minutes, 08:45 to 17:10; about 300 to 350 yen, so check the price.

places.name: Hokkaido Shrine (Hokkaido Jingu)
places.note: Founded in 1869 and home to four deities including Emperor Meiji, in the woods of Maruyama Park with the zoo next door. Free and open at all hours; a goshuin stamp is 300 yen, and 40 minutes is enough.

places.name: Hohei Kan
places.note: Opened in 1881 as a government hotel, said to be the oldest wooden hotel in Japan, and the Meiji Emperor slept in the Murasaki room. 09:00 to 17:00, Friday to 20:00, about 2 dollars, so check the price; the ground-floor videos are Japanese only.

places.name: Botanic Garden, Hokkaido University
places.note: Founded in 1886, with an Ainu museum, a small museum of local animals and two greenhouses. 420 yen, Tuesday to Sunday 09:00 to 15:30, closed Monday; in winter only the greenhouse may be open, so November hours vary, check.

places.name: Hokkaido Museum
places.note: The island's natural and human history in one building, with the best Ainu galleries in Sapporo, English labels and multilingual audio guides. About 5 dollars, 09:30 to 16:30, closed Monday; give it two to three hours and pair it with the Historical Village in the same forest.

places.name: Teppan Okonomiyaki Masaya
places.note: Okonomiyaki on the iron five minutes from the station; order the Furano Tama, 1,250 yen on a 2023-24 menu, or the Genghis Khan yakisoba, so check the price. 11:30 to 14:30 and 17:00 to 20:30, closed Thursday, Friday if Thursday is a holiday.

places.name: Furano Jam Garden
places.note: A jam maker's garden in the hills east of town, free to walk round, 45 minutes. Listed 09:00 to 17:30 and open all year, but November hours were not confirmed, so hours vary, check.

places.name: Namishibuki (Sea Spray)
places.note: Salt ramen, char siu, yakitori and crisp chicken skin five minutes' walk from the bus terminal. 11:00 to 14:30 and 17:30 to 20:15, closed Sunday; Tabelog gives only an undated 1,000 to 2,999 yen band, so check the price, and winter opening is not confirmed.

places.name: Otaru City General Museum
places.note: Built on the roots of Hokkaido's first railway of 1880, with the Meiji steam locomotive Shizuka and a planetarium. 300 yen in winter, 400 in summer, 09:30 to 17:00, closed Tuesday; the 300 yen Canal Hall has full-size Meiji and Taisho street scenes.

places.name: Former Nippon Yusen Otaru Branch
places.note: A 1906 Renaissance-style stone shipping office, an Important Cultural Property, with a ship model downstairs and the banquet hall upstairs from the film Love Letter. 300 yen, 25 minutes, 09:30 to 17:00, closed Tuesday; it reopened after renovation, so confirm.

places.name: Former JNR Temiya Line
places.note: The rails of the Horonai line, Hokkaido's first railway of 1880, passengers to 1962 and freight to 1985, now a free walking trail open at all hours. Go at dusk; it is snowy now, and the Snow Light Path lanterns are in February.

places.name: Suitengu Shrine
places.note: A water-god shrine founded in 1859 on a hill over the port and the Sea of Japan, free and usually quiet; go for the sunset, though one visitor found it shut from about 16:00, and the short steep path can be icy now.

places.name: Otaru Nishin Goten, the municipal herring house
places.note: The fishermen's house of the herring years with the nets and tools, on the hill by the lighthouse, 300 yen, listed 09:00 to 16:00. A March 2026 visitor found it shut for winter, so it is likely shut now; check.

places.name: Otaru Music Box Museum
places.note: Free, and three floors that are mostly a shop; the 19th-century French boxes and the Orpheus disc box are on floor 2. Hours vary, check, 09:00 to 18:00 on one listing; go at opening or not at all.

places.name: Arishima Takeo Memorial Museum
places.note: The writer Arishima Takeo gave his father's farm to its tenants in 1922; 600 items and Fujikura's harie landscapes, with a book cafe facing Yotei. 500 yen cash; Monday or Tuesday closures and hours vary by source, check.

places.name: Kutchan Museum of Natural History (Furudokan)
places.note: Settler households, a schoolroom and tools beside the natural history of the valley, 20 minutes on a wet day. 200 yen, shared with the Shu Ogawara art museum next door; 09:00 to 17:00, closed Tuesday.

places.name: Shu Ogawara Museum of Art
places.note: The paintings of Shu Ogawara, born in Kutchan in 1911, with a piano in the lobby and Yotei in the window. 09:00 to 17:00, closed Tuesday; the ticket is shared with the Kutchan museum, so check the price.

places.name: Soga Hokuei Stone Circle
places.note: Five small Jomon stone circles where jadeite and deep pots were dug up, Yotei behind; free, no staff or facilities, muddy in rain, and under snow now, so it is a stop for a clear spring or summer day.

places.name: Kutchan Shrine
places.note: Founded by the settlers in 1896, burnt in 1965 and rebuilt in 1973; free, 06:00 to 20:00 and open in winter. The 28 July festival brings out the Kutchan Akasaka Yakko procession.

places.name: Lerch Memorial Park
places.note: A small free park with the bronze of Lt-Col Theodor von Lerch, called the father of skiing in Hokkaido, and Yotei across the fields; ten minutes is plenty, on the way into Kutchan.

places.name: Lake Hangetsu
places.note: A crescent crater lake at the foot of Yotei with a loop path and lookouts, free, 20 to 30 minutes of walking. In winter it is snowshoes only and the ice is thin, so stay off it.

places.name: Niseko Oyunuma
places.note: A 200 m sulphur pond steaming out about 1,000 litres a minute, free; the smell is strong, and winter access is not confirmed, so check before you drive up.

places.name: Kagami-numa
places.note: A mirror pond with floating islands on Annupuri's north-east slope, 45 to 60 minutes up, free. Bear country, so carry a bell; under snow in winter.

places.name: Furano City Museum
places.note: Eight rooms of Furano's settlement, natural history and postwar life, 12 km south of town. Free, 09:00 to 17:00, closed Monday and 31 December to 5 January; it is poorly heated, so keep your coat on in November.

places.name: Furano Shrine
places.note: Founded in 1902, moved here in 1907, with a 1936 Shinmei-style main hall of Tokyo University forest timber. Free, grounds open at all hours, the goshuin office 09:00 to 17:00.

places.name: Hokkaido Navel Monument
places.note: The stone that marks the geographic centre of Hokkaido, the reason Furano calls itself the navel town; free, in school grounds, and sources put it at two different schools, so check before you walk over.

places.name: Rokugo Forest, the Kita no Kuni kara set
places.note: The log cabins from the 1981 drama Kita no Kuni kara, left as filmed, 25 minutes' drive from the station, free parking. 09:30 to 16:00, last entry 15:30, shut from late November to mid-April; the fee is not listed, so check the price.

places.name: Goto Sumio Museum of Art
places.note: More than 130 Japanese-style paintings by Goto Sumio in gold and platinum, open all winter. 1,210 yen, 10:00 to 16:00 from November, last entry 15:30, one source says 09:00; shut 29 December to 3 January and on exhibit-change days.

places.name: Kamifurano Town Pioneer Memorial Hall
places.note: The Taisho-era Tokachidake eruption mudflow, told in the restored house of Mayor Yoshida, with Ayako Miura's Mudslide Area monument. Weekends 09:00 to 16:00 on one listing, winter not stated, so hours vary, check, and check the price.

places.name: Shiretoko National Park Nature Center
places.note: The park's film, bear spray and gear shop, cafe and the start of the Furepe trail; free, 09:00 to 16:00 from late October, shut Wednesdays in December. Snowshoes and boots are 500 yen each in winter, and no buses run until drift ice.

places.name: Shiretoko World Heritage Conservation Center
places.note: The village visitor centre with life-size brown bear and sika deer models and English films, the wet-day hour in Utoro. Free, 09:00 to 16:30 in winter, closed Tuesday from late October to April and over the year end.

places.name: Oronko Rock
places.note: A 60 m rock at the port, about 170 steps to a 360-degree view, one of the Shiretoko Eight Views; free. Sources disagree on whether it is shut in winter, the steps ice up and broken boards were reported, so check.

places.name: Cape Puyuni
places.note: One of the Eight Views of Shiretoko, the sunset over Utoro port and Oronko Rock, with drift ice below in winter; free, but the roadside parking is small, so arrive before the light goes.

places.name: Yuhidai Observatory
places.note: The sunset deck over the Okhotsk on the hill above the village, another of the Eight Views and lit for the February drift-ice festival; free, hours vary, check.

places.name: Shari Town Shiretoko Museum
places.note: The only real museum in reach, 45 km west in Shari: Jomon and Ainu finds, Shiretoko history and taxidermy. 300 yen, 09:00 to 17:00, closed Monday; it fits on the drive in or out, not as a day.

outings.why: The 3 km ground loop past all five lakes with Rausu-dake behind them, then the 2 km Furepe walk from the Nature Center to a cliff-edge waterfall. Flat, but from 10 May to 31 July you may only walk the ground loop with a registered guide at
outings.name: Shiretoko Goko long loop and Furepe Falls
outings.season: Mid-April to mid-November for the boardwalk; ground loop gui
outings.fallback: The 800 m elevated boardwalk to Lake One is free, fenced against bears and open whatever the weather.

outings.why: A warm sulphur river you wade up barefoot or in rented water shoes, three climbable falls to a fourth where the trail ends. It is 500 metres and takes 30 to 45 minutes up, the road in is 11 km of gravel, and since 2023 you need a timed onli
outings.name: Kamuiwakka hot falls
outings.season: July, August and September; private cars banned and a shuttl
outings.fallback: Drive the gravel road as far as the Iwaobetsu trailhead and turn round; the river itself closes in rain.

outings.why: Forty minutes over the 738 m pass to Rausu, then two and a half hours in the Nemuro Strait for sperm whales, Baird's beaked whales, Pacific white-sided dolphins and orcas in June and July. Sightings are good but not guaranteed and the boats
outings.name: The Rausu whale boat over Shiretoko Pass
outings.season: Late April to mid-October; orcas peak in June and July, sper
outings.fallback: Stop at the pass viewpoint for Yotei-shaped Rausu-dake and Kunashiri, and soak at Kuma no Yu, the free outdoor bath above Rausu.

outings.why: A small Gojiraiwa Kanko boat up the west coast to Rusha Bay, where brown bears fish the river mouth in plain sight; you cannot get there by land. Two hours, wet and cold even in August, and they cancel in a north wind.
outings.name: The Utoro bear boat to Rusha
outings.season: Late April to October; bears most reliable July to September
outings.fallback: The big Aurora ship's 90-minute short course to Kamuiwakka from the same port, which runs in more weather but shows fewer bears.

outings.why: The 1,898 m volcano everything in Niseko faces, climbed from the Makkari trailhead on the gentlest of the four routes, which is still 1,670 m of gain and about nine hours walking with the crater rim at the top. Start by 06:00; the weather t
outings.name: Mt Yotei by the Makkari trail
outings.season: July to September; snow in the crater until late June.
outings.fallback: Shinsen-numa, the boardwalk marsh on the Panorama Line, one flat hour with the same mountain in view.

outings.why: Twenty-five minutes up the Panorama Line to a boardwalk loop round a high marsh and pond, then back down to the sulphur baths at Goshiki. The road is shut by snow from late October to late April.
outings.name: Shinsen-numa and Goshiki Onsen
outings.fallback: Kyogoku Fukidashi Park, where Yotei's meltwater comes out of the rock, twenty minutes the other way.

outings.name: Farm Tomita and Lavender East
outings.season: Late June to early August; peak mid to late July. Lavender E
outings.fallback: Furano Cheese Factory and the winery, both open year round.

outings.season: May to October for colour; the pond is lit at night from Nov
outings.fallback: Blue Pond and Shirahige only, from the Furano side, two hours.

outings.why: Thirty-five minutes by train along the coast, then a flat 4 km loop of stone warehouses, the Bank of Japan branch and the glass shops, with an uni or sushi lunch in the middle. It is the most-visited day trip in Hokkaido and Sakaimachi is s
outings.name: Otaru on foot: the canal, Sakaimachi and sushi street

outings.fallback: Skip Sakaimachi and take the ropeway up Tenguyama for the harbour.

destination.name: Hokkaido
destination.pitch: In summer Hokkaido is the only part of Japan where the point is the outdoors and the food is better for it; nine days is enough for the lavender, the far northeast peninsula and one volcano, as long as you fly out of a different airport tha
destination.caveat: This pack assumes July to early September, with a rental car from Sapporo onward; winter Hokkaido is a different trip entirely, with Niseko's January and February powder, drift ice off Rausu, the Snow Festival in early February, Shiretoko's pass and Kamuiwakka shut and the Furano fields under snow. Put together for you just now from a live search, so check anything you're pinning the trip on.

because.city: Sapporo is a grid city with a decent subway, a bar district that runs until five in the morning and the best cheap eating in the north, but it is one base, not the trip.
because.food: Soup curry, Genghis Khan lamb on a domed grill, miso ramen from the shop that invented it, June-to-August uni from Shakotan, Furano cheese and Niseko milk, all of it cheaper than Tokyo.
because.nature: Shiretoko is a World Heritage peninsula with a road that stops halfway, brown bears on the beach at Rusha, and a hot river you wade up; the Daisetsuzan side and Yotei are volcanoes you can actually walk on.
because.culture: Thin, and honest to say so: the Bank of Japan's Otaru branch, the pioneer village at Nopporo and Noguchi's park are the whole list, and none of them takes more than two hours.
because.adventure: Mt Yotei by the Makkari trail is nine hours and 1,670 metres, Kamuiwakka is a barefoot scramble up a warm river, and the small-boat bear cruise from Utoro goes where the road does not.
because.relaxation: Every base has a sulphur spring within twenty minutes, and the Utoro onsen hotels put you in an outdoor bath facing the Sea of Okhotsk with nothing to do after dinner.
because.exploration: Five bases, each doing something the last one did not: a city of two million, a herring port, a farming valley, a ski village in its off-season, and a fishing town at the end of Route 334.
